extracted.intended_audience: prospective Damon Runyon Fellowship applicants (postdoctoral and physician-scientist candidates), their Sponsors, and institutional administrative officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and review criteria for applying to the Damon Runyon Fellowship Award (postdoctoral and physician-scientist training fellowships), including eligibility, application requirements, funding terms, reporting, and award policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the research proposal (importance of the problem, originality of approach, appropriateness of techniques and clarity of presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate importance of problem addressed, how original the approach is, whether the proposed techniques are appropriate, and how clearly the proposal is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and productivity of candidate and Sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualifications, experience and productivity of both the candidate and the Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess track record, mentorship capability of Sponsor, and evidence that candidate and Sponsor can carry out the proposed program and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the research training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the research training environment in which the proposed research is to be conducted and its potential for broadening and strengthening the candidate's ability to independently conduct innovative and substantive research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed environment should represent a new opportunity to expand the candidate's scientific skill set; direct extensions of the candidate's graduate work (in approach, technique or exact area of study) will not be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor mentorship and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must apply under the guidance of a Sponsor — a scientist (tenured, tenure-track or equivalent position) capable of providing mentorship to the Fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor is expected to aid in planning, execution and supervision, foster development of Fellow's knowledge, technical and analytical skills, capacity for inquiry, and assist in career goals. No more than two Damon Runyon Fellows may be funded to work with the same Sponsor at any given time (including Co-Sponsors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconscious bias awareness in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are instructed to be aware of potential unconscious biases when reviewing, scoring and discussing candidates and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement is read at review sessions reminding reviewers that acknowledging unconscious bias can help combat its negative impact on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and renewal contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are granted for a four-year term with second-, third- and fourth-year funding contingent upon satisfactory progress reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress is monitored via required reports at specified months; satisfactory review is required for continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at Fellows' Retreats
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows in their first and third years of funding will attend Damon Runyon Fellows' Retreats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retreats are designed to foster collaboration and interaction between scientists across fields relevant to cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: No indirect costs or institutional overhead
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of this grant can be used for indirect costs or institutional overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to institutions for support of the Fellow, but the grant does not cover institutional overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend and expense allowance amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend schedule (Year 1: $70,000; Year 2: $72,000; Year 3: $74,000; Year 4: $76,000) and annual expense allowance of $2,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expense allowance is awarded to the laboratory and can be used by the Fellow for educational and scientific expenses; with written request it may be used for health benefits. It is not for institutional overhead, registration fees, or fellowship taxes. Institutions may not automatically deduct fees without the Fellow's approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense allowance permitted uses and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Expense allowance may be used for educational and scientific expenses, travel (coach class for plane/train), supplies, and other limited categories; equipment over $1,500 must be itemized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used for travel, provide meeting name/location, dates, and use of funds. For supplies, list general categories. Equipment costing $1,500+ must include item name, date, and price. Equipment purchased becomes property of the Awardee. Only allowable 'other' purchases: health insurance (if requested), scientific subscriptions, or items approved by the Foundation. Fellows must submit an Expense Allowance Usage Form and annual Financial Expenditure Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation and other support restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementation of stipends is permitted from the host institution or sponsor’s grants, but not by any other fellowship awards or grants. Fellows are permitted to obtain additional awards or grants to cover research expenses only and are not permitted to hold any other award or grant that supplements their stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total stipend should not exceed level of support for other professionals at the same level at the institution. Fellows must seek Foundation approval before applying for any other award or grant. Budgetary overlap is not allowed; current and pending support must be reported and relationships to the Damon Runyon-funded project explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time research expectation and time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon Fellowship awards are intended for full-time research; Level 1 applicants expected to devote 100% of their time; physician-scientists must devote at least 80% of their time to Damon Runyon-supported research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities constituting the remaining percentage must be clearly specified in the application and annual progress report for physician-scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on pursuing degrees during fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon Fellows are not permitted to pursue additional degrees during the course of their fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deviation (e.g., attempting to pursue a degree) would conflict with full-time research expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: required degrees and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have completed one or more of the following degrees or its equivalent: MD, PhD, MD/PhD, DDS, DVM, DO. The applicant must include a copy of their diploma to confirm date of conferral (or formal graduate school letter if PhD requirements completed but diploma pending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree conferral date is used for other eligibility timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 1 timing and prior lab tenure restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 1 (basic and physician-scientists): must have received their degrees no more than 18 months prior to the application deadline date and must not have been in their Sponsor's labs for more than one year prior to the application deadline; expected to devote 100% time to Damon Runyon research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions aim to target early postdoctoral researchers/new trainees; applicants must document dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level 2 physician-scientist eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Physician-scientist applicants must have completed residencies and clinical training, be board eligible in the United States at the start date of the Fellowship, and be able to devote at least 80% of their time to Damon Runyon-supported research activities. Applicants may apply prior to initial assistant professorship appointment; postdocs, clinical fellows and clinical instructors are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates holding or awarded NIH K awards at the time of application are not eligible; candidates holding institutional K12 awards may apply but must turn back K12 funding if awarded a Damon Runyon Fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on applications and Fellows per Sponsor/institution
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than two Damon Runyon Fellows will be funded to work with the same Sponsor at any given time (including Co-Sponsors). Only one fellowship application will be accepted from a Sponsor or Fellow per review session (including Co-Sponsors); there is no limit to the number of applications from an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits are per review session; co-sponsorship counts toward Sponsor limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification for prior accepted fellowships or ongoing degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates who have already accepted a postdoctoral research fellowship award are not eligible. Candidates pursuing a degree are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may hold a T32 at time of application but not concurrently with the Damon Runyon Fellowship Award if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on continuing in same lab or direct extension of graduate work
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral training in the same institution in which the applicant received their degree is discouraged, particularly if in the same department. Proposals to continue training in the laboratory where the applicant received their PhD will not be considered. Proposals that are direct extensions of graduate work will not be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applying to stay in same institution/department or lab, applicant must address reasons in application; such proposals are discouraged and likely ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional site and special cases for for-profit or government labs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research must be conducted at a university, hospital or research institution. Candidates working in a structured postdoctoral research program at a for-profit institution may apply; if awarded the for-profit institution will pay the Fellow's salary directly and Damon Runyon will supplement if institutional salary is less. Candidates applying to work in foreign-based or United States government laboratories may be awarded a fellowship if the program represents an unusual opportunity. Foreign candidates may apply to do their research only in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must adhere to same privileges/responsibilities and Fellowship guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreements restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may not enter into confidentiality agreements that prevent or delay them from publishing and/or presenting their Damon Runyon-supported research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any confidentiality agreement that restricts timely dissemination conflicts with award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: timing and technical/lay report content
rubrics_metrics.description: Second-, third- and fourth-year funding is contingent on satisfactory annual progress reports. At the end of months 11, 23 and 35 Fellows must submit a detailed progress report including a technical summary (signed by Fellow and Sponsor, ≤3 pages), a lay abstract (≤1 page), bibliography of publications (pdfs), list of conferences/presentations, description of collaborations, participation in outreach/mentorship, a sponsor letter assessing progress, completed IP disclosure form, expense allowance usage form, and request for OA fee reimbursement if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical summary should be targeted to a general scientific audience and sufficiently detailed to clearly articulate activities; all reports are kept confidential and are used to audit progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At completion of the fellowship, submit a detailed final progress report including a technical summary (≤3 pages), two abstracts (one lay and one scientific), bibliography of all publications from the research (pdfs), list of conferences/seminars, collaborations description, outreach activities, a statement indicating how the award made a difference, a statement of future plans, an up-to-date CV, a brief sponsor summary assessing progress, completed IP disclosure form, and request for OA fee reimbursement if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final report documents outcomes across the entire fellowship term and is required for closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial recordkeeping and reporting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution's financial officer must maintain a separate account including receipts for each fellowship, available for audit. Reports of expenditures on Foundation forms must be submitted within 60 days of the end of each award year. Any unexpended expense allowance may be carried over, but any unexpended stipend must be returned at the end of each fellowship year. Upon termination or expiration, final report of expenditures with refund of unexpended balance must be submitted within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Damon Runyon Fellowship Financial Expenditure Report form and indicate any carry-over in the specified row. Pre-award spending is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed travel and expenditure details for Financial Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If the expense allowance was used for travel, report the name/location of meeting, dates, and restricted uses (registration fee, lodging, meals, transportation—coach class only for plane/train). For supplies, list general categories. Equipment costing $1,500 or more must include item name, date, and price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment purchased with Damon Runyon funds becomes the property of the Awardee. The Foundation lists only specific allowable 'other' purchases; contact the office for approval of any item not listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent child allowance policy and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation provides a Dependent Child Allowance of $1,000 per child per year. Eligible Fellows must submit a dependent child allowance form and a copy of the birth or adoption certificate for each child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Dependent Child Allowance must be reported as received in the annual financial report, but the Foundation does not require reporting on how it is spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and presentations acknowledgment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications (including abstracts of presentations) resulting from Foundation-supported projects must carry the acknowledgment: "[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon Fellow supported by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (DRG-#[___])."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees should identify themselves as Damon Runyon Fellows in presentations and on websites and may use the Foundation logo on slides, posters, and websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan repayment program eligibility and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will retire up to $100,000 of qualifying medical school debt for awardees; qualified candidates must first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program to be eligible for Damon Runyon repayment. Qualifying loans are those for tuition and direct educational expenses incurred during medical school (not loans for living expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must submit documentation within one month of award acceptance and annually; payments are made to lenders up to $25,000 per year (aggregate $100,000). Consolidated loans require agreements for underlying loans. Repayments stop during leaves unless written permission granted. Loans not qualifying include loans from individuals, delinquent/defaulted loans, or fees/penalties. Loan repayments are taxable income; Foundation will approximate and pay an Additional Tax Payment to offset increased tax liability. If the Fellow terminates early, Foundation may require repayment of amounts paid unless Fellow continues cancer research; payback may be waived at Foundation's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa status and compliance responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institution is responsible for ensuring awardees comply with federal immigration policy. If a Fellow’s visa status changes or expires preventing them from working at the designated institution, Damon Runyon must be notified immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify may result in immediate termination of the award and may jeopardize future awards to the institution and/or Sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award administration and non-negotiable Foundation policies
rubrics_metrics.description: All awardees must adhere to the terms of the Foundation's award statement and invention policy; the Foundation will not modify the terms of its policies at the request of individual institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to the sponsoring institution; an award does not constitute an employer-employee relationship between the Foundation and the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedure and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, log into Altum | Proposal Central and search for Damon Runyon Fellowship Award. Applications are due by 4:00 pm Eastern Time on August 14, 2026. Application instructions and forms are located on the Foundation's application pages and within Proposal Central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online submission procedures and include required forms (diploma, sponsor letters, etc.).
